newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan's Fuji Heavy in China car venture.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Fuji Heavy in China car venture.

text.p: Japan's Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd will invest 294 million yuan ($35.4 million) for a 49 percent stake in a car-making joint venture in China, a spokesman for the Chinese partner said on Monday.
The joint venture with Guizhou Yunque (Lark) Car Corp in the southwestern province of Guizhou would have an annual production capacity of 10,000 compact cars, the spokesman said.
The capacity would eventually be boosted to 300,000 units, the spokesman said without elaborating.
The Chinese side has pledged to pour 306 million yuan into the joint venture for a 51 percent stake, he said.
Fuji Heavy Industries signed a letter of intent with China Guizhou Aviation Industrial Corp and China Guizhou Joint Automotive Industrial Corp last month to set up the joint venture.

"The new company will carry out technical renovation on the existing production lines in a bid to produce and sell quality Yunque cars," the China Daily quoted Yang Binyan, general manager of China Guizhou Joint Automotive Industrial Corp, as saying.
The car's local content rate would be increased to reduce costs, Yang said.
The Chinese carmaker currently uses Fuji Heavy technology and equipment.
The newspaper gave no further details.
Guizhou Yunque is one of eight car makers that has the backing of the government.

The government plans to pool more than 100 billion yuan by the year 2000 to build the eight sedan and mini-car manufacturers into a pillar industry yielding over 1,000 billion yuan in annual output value.
Fuji Heavy makes Subaru brand cars.
